design: Within-course Alternative Uses Task; AI-assisted second round
key_finding: AI-assisted paper-clip brainstorming scored higher for originality (7.53 vs 5.47), flexibility (7.55 vs 6.01), fluency (10.84 vs 8.00) and elaboration (25.96 vs 20.45).
limit: Short task and fixed sequence; results are exploratory and do not prove long-term gains.

design: Preregistered experiment; AI-assisted vs unaided creative problem-solving
classification: Positive on solution quality and originality
key_finding: AI assistance improved solution quality (d=0.69), elaboration (d=0.61), originality (d=0.55) and task self-efficacy (d=0.65).
limit: A short experimental task does not establish sustained creative development.

classification: Mixed; no overall evidence of decline
key_finding: 25% of analysed students decreased, 21.43% stayed unchanged and 53.57% improved on the creativity measure; the overall change was not statistically significant.
limit: Small convenience sample and no control group; the study cannot establish causation.

classification: Mixed; effects depended on discipline and dimension
key_finding: ChatGPT tended to improve fluency and elaboration in Marketing and Management, while effects were little or absent in Entrepreneurship; originality gains were inconsistent.
limit: Business disciplines may not represent all subjects; the type of task matters.

classification: Mixed; creativity preserved but ideas converged semantically
key_finding: AI did not reduce fluency, flexibility or originality, but semantic divergence was lower and AI-assisted ideas more often resembled existing products; early AI use was associated with stronger later unaided ideation.
limit: Idea-level observations are not the same as independent student counts; data were not publicly released with the article.

design: Preregistered laboratory experiment with creative picture-idea tasks
classification: Positive on average; benefit varied by baseline creative potential
key_finding: Access to ChatGPT raised average creative performance by 0.24 points (0.32 SD, p<.01) versus human-only work; students with moderate baseline creative potential benefited most.
limit: Laboratory tasks and short-term outcomes do not fully capture classroom learning or long-run originality.
